learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Locate computer science within engineering disciplines.
Understand the fundamentals of the binary system to comprehend information representation in computers.
Identify hardware components that constitute a computer system, as well as their interconnection in networks, and understand their basic operation.
Distinguish the main peripherals used in a computer system and specifically in the field of engineering.
Classify the different types of software used in a computer system.
Identify and classify different types of computer systems and their application domains.
Understand the main functions performed by an operating system.
Analyze which services the operating system provides to programs and end-users.
Identify the main operating systems used in professional engineering environments and use the main services at user level.
Understand the main functions performed by a database management system.
Create data models for simple problems.
Use basic expressions to retrieve and modify information stored in a database.
Identify which database management systems are used in professional engineering environments.
Identify the main application programs used in professional engineering environments.
Understand the concept of algorithm and the process of abstracting a problem in programming.
Identify the program development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Recognize the elementary data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Manage the elementary control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract operations.
Design small applications to solve elementary problems in collaborative work environments.

syllabus_topics: INT - Introduction
Overview of computer science, in the context of other engineering disciplines
Structure and operation of a computer
Information representation in a computer
BD - Introduction to databases
Concept of database
Fundamentals of the relational data model
Performing queries and modifications
Database Management Systems in professional engineering environments
PRO - Introduction to programming
Abstraction of problems for programming: fundamental concepts
Variables, expressions, assignment
Using console input/output
Handling basic flow control structures: sequential, alternative, and repetitive
Definition and use of subprograms and functions. Variable scope
File input/output
Basic data types and structures
Program development processes. From high-level to execution on the processor. Compiled languages and interpreted languages
HSW - Hardware and software components of a computer system
Structure and operation of a computer: Von Neumann Architecture and machine language
Peripheral devices
System interconnection: types, mechanisms, and applications
Types of software: system software and application software
Types of computer systems and their application domains
SO - Introduction to operating systems
Concept and functions performed by an operating system
Interface and services offered to programs
Interface and services offered to users
Operating systems used in professional engineering environments
Introduction to laboratory tools. The spreadsheet as a tool
Design, implementation, and exploitation of a database
Programming with Python
Introduction to the development environment
Variables, expressions, and console input-output
Flow control: if-else, while, for
Functions
Structures: lists and strings
Files

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical exam (covering all content, weighted by topic)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the theoretical block requires at least 40% in Topic 3 (Programming) and an overall score greater than 4 out of 10 to average with the practical block. The practical block requires at least 40% in Topic 3 (Programming) and an overall score greater than 4 out of 10 to average with the theoretical block. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 50% Theoretical block score + 50% Practical block score; otherwise, the final grade is the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary assessment, the minimum scores for both theoretical and practical blocks must be greater than or equal to 5 out of 10 to average; the extraordinary exam will be the same as the ordinary, and previous scores (>=5.0) can be carried over. If minimums are not met, the final grade is the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0.
